questions.question: What happens if you refuse to take an alcohol test when suspected of drunk driving?

options.text: It is your right and there are no consequences.
You will only receive a fine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your license will be suspended.
questions.explanation: When you drive in Texas, you automatically agree to take an alcohol test whenever police ask. You cannot be forced to take the test, but your license will be suspended immediately if you refuse.

questions.question: You should not park within ____ of a traffic control signal.
questions.correctAnswerText: 30 feet
questions.explanation: Do not park within 30 feet of a traffic control signal like a stop sign, flashing light, or yield sign. Parking too close can cause accidents.

questions.question: You turn onto a two-lane road with a broken yellow line in the middle. What does this tell you?

options.text: You must stay to the left of the broken yellow lines.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road goes both directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow centerlines separate traffic going in opposite directions. A broken line means you can cross it to pass slower traffic when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do if traffic lights are not working at an intersection?

options.text: Park your vehicle off the road and wait for power to return.
Use hand signals to show other drivers what you plan to do.
Turn on hazard lights and drive through without stopping.
Treat it like a four-way stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, act as if it is a four-way stop. Yield to other drivers, and when it is your turn, go through carefully.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: A railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: What helps drivers save gas?

options.text: Letting the car run in the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down gradually.
questions.explanation: Every time you brake hard, you waste fuel speeding back up. Drivers who look ahead can slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid sudden braking. This saves gas.

questions.question: What do downward-pointing triangular signs mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to other traffic.
questions.explanation: Downward-pointing triangular signs tell drivers to yield. Wait until the road is clear of traffic and pedestrians, then you can go.

questions.question: Why should you be careful when passing a bicycle?

options.text: You are moving faster than the bicycle.
The bicycle always has the right-of-way.
Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass.
The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid something on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid something on the road.
questions.explanation: Be careful when passing a bicycle because the cyclist may suddenly swerve into traffic to avoid an object. Always drive carefully near cyclists.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when behind a large vehicle blocking your view, in bad weather or heavy traffic, when exiting a highway, when following a motorcycle or bicycle, and when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: What happens if a driver or passenger does not wear a safety belt?

options.text: A fine for each person not wearing a safety belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: A fine for each person not wearing a safety belt.
questions.explanation: In Texas, drivers can get a ticket for not wearing a safety belt and for not having children under 17 in a safety seat or belt. Anyone 15 or older can be ticketed for not wearing a safety belt. There are no exceptions to this law.

questions.question: You see a flashing yellow light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to change.
Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
Drive slowly and carefully through the intersection.
Get ready to stop; the light is about to turn red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly and carefully through the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you can go, but you must drive slowly and watch for other traffic. Look both ways before entering the intersection.

questions.question: If you feel worried, nervous, angry, or upset, what should you do as a driver?

options.text: Drive normally; your emotions won't affect your driving.
Drive faster because you are more alert.
Calm down and focus on driving before you start the engine.
Call a friend to talk while you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Calm down and focus on driving before you start the engine.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions can distract you from driving safely. Your mind may be thinking about other things instead of the road. Always calm yourself first and get focused before you start driving.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, what should you do?

options.text: Let drivers already on the highway go first.
Assume other drivers will move for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let drivers already on the highway go first.
questions.explanation: When entering a highway, you must let drivers already on it go first. Merge safely into traffic when you have a safe opening.

questions.question: How should you pass a person riding a bicycle?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn them you are passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane to get around them.
Slow down and give them plenty of space.
Speed up and pull in front of them quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them plenty of space.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists have less protection than drivers. Always slow down and give them as much space as possible. Passing too quickly can cause them to lose control.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks are allowed on the upcoming narrow bridge.
The bridge ahead is open to one-way traffic only.
Only one car can use the bridge at a time.
The bridge ahead may be too narrow to pass a truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bridge ahead may be too narrow to pass a truck.
questions.explanation: This warning sign tells drivers that a narrow bridge is ahead. You may not have enough space to pass a truck on this bridge, so be careful and slow down.

questions.question: What does a red traffic light mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: A red light means you must stop. You must stop at the stop line, before any crosswalk, and before entering the intersection.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: When you see a child about to run into the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a child about to run into the street.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn drivers or pedestrians of danger when they may not see you. For example, honk if a child is about to run into the street in front of you.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are separated by ____ lines.
questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: When making a right turn, you should NOT:

options.text: Turn too wide in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn too wide in your lane.
questions.explanation: Always signal and slow down before turning right. Move to the right lane. Do not swing too wide, as this can hit other vehicles.

questions.question: What is the "No zone"?

options.text: The blind spots around trucks and buses.
An area with rules about stereo volume.

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spots around trucks and buses.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have large blind spots on all sides, in front, and in back. Your car cannot be seen in these blind spots. These areas are called the "No zone."

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic is coming from both directions ahead.

questions.question: If another car is about to hit you, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Sound your horn.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians when they may not see you. If you think another driver is about to hit you, sound your horn.

questions.question: After an accident, what should you provide?

options.text: Help to anyone who is injured.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before leaving an accident scene, give the other drivers your name, address, registration, and insurance information. Help anyone who is injured.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, what must a driver do?

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees you.
Always give them the right-of-way, even if they are in the wrong.
Give them the right-of-way only when they have the legal right to it.
Slow down and honk near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always give them the right-of-way, even if they are in the wrong.
questions.explanation: You must do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian or another vehicle, no matter what. Always watch for pedestrians and give them the right-of-way, even if they are crossing where they should not.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: Drive through if there is no other traffic.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light is used at dangerous intersections. Treat it the same as a stop sign.

questions.question: When is it okay to honk your horn?

options.text: When you have to stop quickly.
When you are passing another car.
When you lose control of your car.
When you are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you lose control of your car.
questions.explanation: It is appropriate to use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. Sound your horn to alert other drivers.

questions.question: In Texas, when must drivers use their headlights?

options.text: When their vehicle has a problem.
30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise.
During the day in clear weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise.
questions.explanation: Slow down when driving at night and make sure you can stop within the distance your headlights shine. You must use your headlights 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise.

questions.question: What do diagonal stripes sloping downward to the right on a barricade mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Go to the right.
questions.explanation: Diagonal stripes on a barricade guide you in which direction to go. Stripes sloping down and to the right mean go to the right. Stripes sloping down and to the left mean go to the left.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Drive at the maximum speed limit.
Drive no faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: You must use your headlights when you cannot see at least 500 feet ahead. Use low beams in fog or rain. High beams will reflect light back into your eyes and make visibility worse.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped with flashing lights. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down and change lanes away from the vehicle if you can do so safely.
Move to the right side of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane and drive at the same speed.
Speed up to pass the vehicle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and change lanes away from the vehicle if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside assistance vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes to give it space. If you cannot change lanes safely, slow down below the speed limit and give the vehicle as much room as possible. Always slow down and be ready to stop at an emergency scene.
